**Aster Design System** — Standardize product UI primitives across three web apps.

**Stack:** node-library • typescript • tests: vitest, testing-library

**Project type:** `design-system`

> Source of truth: `.project-spine/spine.json` (hash `045611f6e141e981`). Every rule below has a traceable source. If a rule is wrong, fix the upstream input (`brief.md`, repo state, or `design-rules.md`) and rerun `spine compile`.

## Repo conventions

- TypeScript strict mode is on. Never use `any`; prefer `unknown` + narrow at the boundary.

## Do / Don't

- Prefer small, focused diffs. One concern per PR or patch.
- Always show the exact test or typecheck command you ran and its result.
- When following a rule from this file, cite it by section heading so reviewers can audit.
- Do not refactor code unrelated to the task, even if it looks better.
- Do not add new dependencies without flagging the choice and reason.
- Add a story, an axe test, and a docs entry whenever a primitive is added or changed.
- Do not introduce hardcoded colors, radii, or spacings in primitives — reference tokens only.
- Do not import app-level code into the design system.

## Never do this (unsafe)

- Never modify generated files (anything under `dist/`, `build/`, `.next/`, or marked `@generated`).
- Never edit lockfiles manually.
- Never commit secrets. Redact any `.env*` content that appears in logs or diffs.
- Never fork a token inside a primitive; update it at the token layer.

## File placement

- Stories live next to components as `*.stories.tsx`.

## Response expectations

- Before claiming work is complete, run the repo's typecheck and test commands and show the output.
- If the brief is ambiguous on a specific section, ask rather than guess. Cite the section heading.

## Component & design rules

- Every primitive exposes a stable, documented prop API. Breaking changes require a deprecation notice and a major bump.
- Primitives never own business logic or data fetching.
- Composition over configuration: prefer slot props over boolean flags when a consumer might need more control.
- Every shared UI component must have at least one Storybook story covering default and loading/error states where applicable.
- Token schema — colors, spacing, radius, motion, typography; all values live as tokens.
- Primitive set — Button, Input, Field, Select, Checkbox, Radio, Switch, Tooltip, Dialog, Toast.
- Layout primitives — Stack, Inline, Grid, Box with consistent spacing scale.
- Icon set — single source, tree-shakeable, accessible by default (role, title).
- Theme surfaces — light/dark/high-contrast themes wired through tokens.

Design rules (from `design-rules.md`):
- All color, spacing, radius, and typography values live as tokens. No raw hex, px, or font-family in components.
- Tokens are the only safe cross-cut between themes; component styles always read from token references.
- Token names are semantic (color.surface.default) not presentational (color.gray-100).
- Every primitive exposes a stable, documented prop API. Breaking changes require a deprecation notice and a major bump.
- Primitives never own business logic or data fetching.
- Composition over configuration: prefer slot props over boolean flags when a consumer might need more control.
- Motion defaults under 200ms; anything longer needs a rationale (progress, context change).
- Every state transition has a stable from → to mapping; avoid intermediate flicker.
- Focus is visible for keyboard users; mouse users get the hover treatment instead.
- All interactive primitives meet WCAG 2.2 AA at default and dense sizes.
- Focus trap inside modals, restoring focus to trigger on close.
- Announce async state changes to screen readers (aria-live polite by default).
- Motion respects prefers-reduced-motion.

## Accessibility baseline

- All interactive elements must be reachable and operable with the keyboard alone.
- Focus must be visible at all times; never remove outlines without replacing them.
- Text contrast must meet WCAG AA (4.5:1 for body, 3:1 for large text).
- Every form control has a programmatic label.
- Pages use proper landmark regions (header, main, nav, footer) and a sensible heading order.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` for any non-essential animation.
- Every interactive primitive exposes a focus ring by default; removal requires an explicit prop.
- Labels, descriptions, and error states are composable via documented slot props.

## UX rules

- Motion defaults under 200ms; anything longer needs a rationale (progress, context change).
- Every state transition has a stable from → to mapping; avoid intermediate flicker.
- Focus is visible for keyboard users; mouse users get the hover treatment instead.
- Props follow a consistent shape across primitives (size, tone, variant, disabled, loading).
- Primitives never embed business logic; they are purely presentational.

## QA guardrails

- Unit tests live next to source as `*.test.ts`. Run `vitest run` in CI and before every commit touching business logic.
- `tsc --noEmit` must pass on every PR.
- Success criterion to verify before launch: Button, Input, Field, Dialog, Tooltip, and Toast ship with docs and tests.
- Success criterion to verify before launch: Axe checks pass for every primitive story.
- Success criterion to verify before launch: First downstream app replaces 80% of raw form controls with primitives.
- Every primitive has at least one Storybook story covering default, hover, focus, disabled, and loading where applicable.
- Visual regression (Chromatic / Playwright snapshots) runs on every PR.
- Axe accessibility check passes per primitive at default and interactive states.
- Bundle-size budget enforced per primitive; new primitives require a budget entry.

## What we are building (from brief)

- Standardize product UI primitives across three web apps.
- Move all color, spacing, radius, and typography decisions into semantic tokens.
- Publish a stable React package with Storybook docs and migration examples.

## Constraints

- React-only v1, TypeScript strict, ESM package output.
- Tokens are exported from Figma as JSON and transformed before publish.
- Downstream apps need light, dark, and high-contrast themes.

## Known risks

- Teams may fork primitives if migration docs are thin.
- Token aliases could drift from Figma unless exports are checked in CI.
